findings.claim: headline accuracy -0.23 % at the design point understates the per-phase error
findings.evidence: per-phase stiffness ratios at ppw=32, A/lambda=0.02 are 0.8098/1.2041/0.8137/1.1920, i.e. single-phase omega errors -10.0 %/+9.8 %/-9.8 %/+9.3 % (worst 10.01 %, at the case tolerance); at ppw=16 the worst phase is 12.05 %, i.e. a single-phase measurement would FAIL the case's own 10 % gate while the reported ensemble mean is -2.48 %. The reported -0.23 % is the mean of two oppositely biased lattice phases.
findings.impact: supported claim = '4-phase ensemble mean within 4.3 % over ppw 16..48'; unsupported claim = 'operator error 0.2 %'; single-phase error reaches 10.0-12.1 % (still below the platform 15 % unacceptability line, so a reporting defect, not a physics failure)

findings.claim: gate D (sigma linearity, 0.000 % spread) is non-discriminating
findings.evidence: dp_measured and dp_theory both carry sigma as a factor (run.py:217-220), so the ratio is sigma-invariant by construction; probe json sigma_ladder shows three bit-identical rows incl. identical std 0.19319821894168854
findings.impact: one of four gates carries no information; also, because omega_got = omega_ref*sqrt(ratio), the measurement cannot detect a wrong k/rho exponent

findings.claim: the A/lambda=0.01 point (-36.7 %) is a quadrature null, not nonlinear detuning as the summary states
findings.evidence: at ppw=32 two of four phases return stiffness_ratio = -0.0 (dp_meas = 0 to machine precision) and the other two +1.61/+1.59; at ppw=16 all four phases are null; std equals mean (0.8016) exactly because of the 0/1.6 mixture
findings.impact: the case's stated failure mode ('out of the linear-response band') mislabels an aliasing artifact of the modal projection; a null phase is a diagnostic that the projection can cancel identically
